hints: Total mass of car and trailer is $1500 + 750 = 2250\text{ kg}$.
Calculate the initial and final kinetic energies at speeds $30\text{ m s}^{-1}$ and $20\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Calculate the gain in potential energy: $mgh = 2250(10)(800 \times 0.08)$.
Calculate the work done against resistances: $(400 + 200) \times 800$, and set up the work-energy balance to find driving force $F_D$.
walkthrough:
Calculate kinetic energy at the bottom ($v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$) and top ($v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$) for the combined mass $m = 2250\text{ kg}$:
$$E_{k, \text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2}(2250)(30^2) = 1125 \times 900 = 1012500\text{ J}$$
$$E_{k, \text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}(2250)(20^2) = 1125 \times 400 = 450000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the potential energy gained with vertical rise $h = 800\sin\alpha = 800(0.08) = 64\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 2250(10)(64) = 1440000\text{ J}$$

Calculate the work done against total resistance force $R = 400 + 200 = 600\text{ N}$ over $800\text{ m}$:
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = 600 \times 800 = 480000\text{ J}$$

Apply the work-energy balance: Work Done by Driving Force + Initial KE = Final KE + Gain in PE + Work Done against Resistance:
$$F_D(800) + 1012500 = 450000 + 1440000 + 480000$$
$$800 F_D + 1012500 = 2370000$$
$$800 F_D = 2370000 - 1012500 = 1357500$$
$$F_D = \frac{1357500}{800} = 1696.875 \approx 1700\text{ N}$$

ai_rubric.Applying the Work–Energy Principle: Calculates KE change, PE gain $= 1440000\text{ J}$, WD against friction $= 480000\text{ J}$, and solves $800(DF) + 1012500 = 2370000$ to get $DF = 1700\text{ N}$.

teacher_walkthrough: Identify all energy components for the combined system of car and trailer ($m = 1500 + 750 = 2250\text{ kg}$) over the $d = 800\text{ m}$ slope:

1. Initial kinetic energy at the bottom of the hill ($u = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$E_{k, \text{initial}} = \frac{1}{2}(2250)(30^2) = 1125 \times 900 = 1012500\text{ J}$$

2. Final kinetic energy at the top of the hill ($v = 20\text{ m s}^{-1}$):
$$E_{k, \text{final}} = \frac{1}{2}(2250)(20^2) = 1125 \times 400 = 450000\text{ J}$$

3. Gravitational potential energy gained, where vertical elevation is $h = d\sin\alpha = 800 \times 0.08 = 64\text{ m}$:
$$\Delta E_p = mgh = 2250 \times 10 \times 64 = 1440000\text{ J}$$

4. Work done against the total non-gravitational resistance ($R = 400 + 200 = 600\text{ N}$):
$$W_{\text{resistance}} = R \times d = 600 \times 800 = 480000\text{ J}$$

State the work-energy principle:
$$W_{\text{driving}} + E_{k, \text{initial}} = E_{k, \text{final}} + \Delta E_p + W_{\text{resistance}}$$
Substitute the computed quantities:
$$F_D(800) + 1012500 = 450000 + 1440000 + 480000$$
$$800 F_D + 1012500 = 2370000$$
Subtract $1012500$ from both sides:
$$800 F_D = 1357500$$
Divide by $800$:
$$F_D = \frac{1357500}{800} = 1696.875\text{ N} \approx 1700\text{ N}$$

hints: On the level road, weight has no horizontal component.
Apply Newton's second law to the combined system: $F_D - R_{\text{total}} = (m_{\text{car}} + m_{\text{trailer}})a$, with $F_D = 2400\text{ N}$ and total resistance $600\text{ N}$.
Apply Newton's second law to the trailer alone: $T - 200 = 750a$ to find the tension $T$.
walkthrough:
Apply Newton's second law horizontally to the combined car-trailer system on the level road with $F_D = 2400\text{ N}$ and total resistance $400 + 200 = 600\text{ N}$:
$$F_D - R_{\text{total}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$2400 - 600 = (1500 + 750)a$$
$$1800 = 2250a$$
$$a = \frac{1800}{2250} = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Apply Newton's second law horizontally to the trailer alone to find tension $T$:
$$T - 200 = 750a$$
$$T - 200 = 750(0.8) = 600$$
$$T = 600 + 200 = 800\text{ N}$$
teacher_walkthrough: On the straight horizontal road at the top of the hill, gravity acts purely vertically and has no component in the direction of motion.

Consider the entire connected system of car and trailer ($m = 2250\text{ kg}$). The internal tension cancels out. Apply Newton's second law:
$$F_{\text{net}} = m_{\text{total}} a$$
$$F_D - R_{\text{car}} - R_{\text{trailer}} = (m_{\text{car}} + m_{\text{trailer}})a$$
Substitute $F_D = 2400\text{ N}$, $R_{\text{car}} = 400\text{ N}$, $R_{\text{trailer}} = 200\text{ N}$, and total mass $2250\text{ kg}$:
$$2400 - 600 = 2250a$$
$$1800 = 2250a$$
Divide by $2250$:
$$a = \frac{1800}{2250} = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Isolate the trailer ($m = 750\text{ kg}$). The forward force is the tension $T$ in the tow-bar and the backward resistance is $200\text{ N}$:
$$T - R_{\text{trailer}} = m_{\text{trailer}} a$$
$$T - 200 = 750(0.8)$$
$$750 \times 0.8 = 600$$
$$T - 200 = 600$$
Add $200$ to both sides:
$$T = 600 + 200 = 800\text{ N}$$
